question: What V/A tradeoff is observed in historical mitigation versions?
caption_claim: Historical P4M newboot acquisition (median/IQR) and separately rendered clean/isolated S/N/P/PN implementations (median/95% conditional bootstrap CI). A common-window service rate is calculated per trial from A completed jobs x 4096 bytes divided by W/50MHz; it is not A full-task throughput. The composition panels are distinct versions/boots.
limitations: Historical loaded-byte identity is unknown; dirty kernels retained.
P4M panel selects only acq29_newboot; earlier acquisitions remain separate.
A rate excludes post-V tail and uses the original fixed-50MHz assumption; independent A full-task completion time is not measured by this panel.
Composition common-window completion counts equal 4096 in these trials, so the derived A rate shares the measured W denominator.
Unified-baseline mitigation reruns remain missing.

question: How does capacity change interference?
caption_claim: Capacity sensitivity in RTL simulation with fixed FIFO behavioral DDR: 16-cycle head startup, then one 8-byte beat/cycle. V complete-task cycles and A walks are shown; V walks are zero in the accepted matrix. Each point is one deterministic configuration; no statistical CI or FPGA timing is inferred.
limitations: Simulation only; model service differs from FPGA DDR.
No repeated trials or bootstrap CI.
A256/V64+2 warmup and the simulation supply model differ from the board campaign; calibration supports qualitative trends only.
